Techniques Used: Naïve Natural Language Processing (NLP) for Concept Generation
Data & Platforms: Large-scale Text Corpora (News, Social Media, Books)

Application Areas: Computational Cultural Evolution and Social Change

Key Research Thinking Patterns: Semantic Vector Mapping of Implicit Cognition: Utilizing dynamic word embeddings (BERT, GPT) and association tests (WEAT) on large-scale text corpora to quantify implicit social biases and track macro-level cultural value shifts over time.

Multidimensional Conceptual Space Modeling: Applying Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and clustering algorithms to cross-lingual datasets to derive universal dimensional frameworks (e.g., FAVEE model) for mapping human social relationship structures.

Longitudinal Trait-State Decomposition: Employing Trait-State-Occasion (TSO) models and multilevel modeling on repeated-measures cohort data to disentangle stable personality traits from state fluctuations in constructs like nostalgia and authenticity.

Neuro-Cultural Convergence: Integrating computational linguistic metrics with fMRI neuroimaging data to validate the neural substrates of culturally derived semantic representations and implicit social cognition.
Summary Description: Huajian Cai is a computational psychologist specializing in the intersection of cultural evolution, social cognition, and personality development. He leverages advanced natural language processing techniques, including dynamic word embeddings and semantic vector arithmetic, to map implicit biases and track macro-level cultural shifts across large-scale corpora. His research uniquely bridges computational linguistics with rigorous psychological assessment, utilizing longitudinal designs and Trait-State-Occasion models to analyze individual development in constructs like nostalgia and authenticity. Furthermore, Cai pioneers multidimensional conceptual space modeling to identify universal dimensions of human social relationships across cultures. By integrating fMRI data with computational semantic analysis, his work provides a comprehensive framework for understanding how macro-cultural forces shape micro-level social cognition and well-being.
